policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'when he was hungry, and they that were with him' renders the verb alone; an added intensive pronoun αὐτός would leave no separate trace in this English, and no note is mapped here.

ASV text has the singular 'how he entered ... and ate the showbread', with the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities read they ate' placing the plural in the margin; that excludes the plural readings r00-base and r01. Between the remaining singular readings, ὃ and οὓς are both simply 'which' in English, so the English does not settle them.
ASV 'a man having a withered hand' is the same English for the participial base and for the RP expansion with ἦν and the article; the added copula is absorbed by the English participle.
θεραπεύειν and θεραπεῦσαι differ only in aspect; ASV 'Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day' renders either infinitive identically.

ASV supplies an explicit future copula, 'What man shall there be of you, that shall have one sheep'; the reading that omits ἔσται yields only 'What man of you ... shall have', with no verb for 'shall there be'.
The variant is Greek word order only; both σου τὴν χεῖρα and τὴν χεῖρά σου are 'thy hand' in ASV, and English word order here is fixed by English grammar.

The readings differ in the position of ἐξελθόντες and in whether the sentence opens with the participle or with Οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι; ASV 'But the Pharisees went out, and took counsel against him' resolves the participle into a finite clause, which it does regardless of the Greek order, so the English does not distinguish them.

ASV reads 'and many followed him', rendering πολλοί with no noun; the reading with ὄχλοι would give 'many multitudes followed him', and ASV renders ὄχλοι as 'multitudes' where it stands (so 12:46, 'speaking to the multitudes').
ἵνα and ὅπως are alike rendered by ASV's purpose clause 'that it might be fulfilled'; the English carries no marker separating them.

ASV 'my servant whom I have chosen' renders the relative alone and leaves any preposition unrepresented, as it does with the Semitic εἰς/ἐν after this verb; the notes here are cross-references, not textual, so εἰς ὅν, ὅν and ἐν ᾧ all remain open.

ASV 'Then was brought unto him one possessed with a demon, blind and dumb' is a passive with a nominative subject, matching προσηνέχθη ... δαιμονιζόμενος τυφλὸς καὶ κωφός; the active plural προσήνεγκαν with accusatives would give 'they brought unto him one possessed'.
ASV 'insomuch that the dumb man spake and saw' names only the dumb man in the result clause; the RP reading τὸν τυφλὸν καὶ κωφὸν καὶ would give 'the blind and dumb man both spake and saw'.
ASV 'And knowing their thoughts he said unto them' has no named subject; the RP reading adds ὁ Ἰησοῦς, which ASV renders as 'Jesus' where it stands (so 12:15, 'And Jesus perceiving it').

The readings differ only in the order of κριταί, ἔσονται and ὑμῶν; ASV 'therefore shall they be your judges' fixes that order by English grammar. The mapped notes are alternative_rendering and a Greek gloss, neither of which bears on a reading.
ἁρπάσαι and its compound διαρπάσαι are both 'spoil his goods' in ASV; the prefix has no separate English exponent here.

ASV closes with an independent future, 'and then he will spoil his house', rather than continuing the ἐὰν μή clause; the aorist subjunctive διαρπάσῃ would fall under that conditional and be rendered 'except he first bind ... and then spoil his house'.

The variant stands at the second ἀφεθήσεται (the first already has τοῖς ἀνθρώποις in the base text). ASV renders the first clause 'shall be forgiven unto men' but the second simply 'shall not be forgiven', with no 'unto men' answering the RP addition.

ASV reads 'neither in this world, nor in that which is to come' — the demonstrative of τούτῳ τῷ αἰῶνι; the RP reading τῷ νῦν αἰῶνι would give 'the world that now is'. The mapped note 'Or, age' is an alternative_rendering of αἰών and does not touch the variant.

ASV has the plain relative 'every idle word that men shall speak'; where ἄν or ἐάν makes a relative indefinite ASV marks it with '-soever' (so 12:32, 'whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of man'). The absence of that marker answers to λαλήσουσιν without ἐάν.
ASV 'Then certain of the scribes and Pharisees answered him, saying' renders the dative αὐτῷ with 'him'; the RP reading omits it, leaving 'answered, saying'.

The readings differ only in whether ἐπιστρέψω precedes or follows its prepositional phrase; ASV 'I will return into my house' is the fixed English order either way. The mapped notes are alternative_rendering.
ASV reads 'he findeth it empty, swept, and garnished', with a pronoun and no noun object; the reading that adds τὸν οἶκον would give 'he findeth the house empty'.

The variant is a καί between the first two participles. ASV's three-item series 'empty, swept, and garnished' punctuates the list in ordinary English style, which neither requires nor excludes the extra connective; no mapped note is textual.

ASV opens 'While he was yet speaking to the multitudes' with no connective, but ASV routinely leaves a transitional δέ in a genitive absolute unrendered, so the bare English does not show whether the particle stood in the text.

ASV prints verse 47 in the text with the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities omit verse 47', which puts the omission in the margin and excludes r02. The two readings that retain the verse are identical in wording, so nothing in the English chooses between them.
λέγοντι and εἰπόντι differ only in tense of the same verb of speaking; ASV 'unto him that told him' renders either participle identically.
